title: Customer QBR Origami Slate and Renewal Sprint Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact QBR deck template set plus an operational renewal sprint playbook. Goal: give CSMs a lightweight, repeatable slate for both Standard (mid-market) and Enterprise accounts that can be adapted in 30–90 minutes before a QBR. Includes a one-page renewal tracker and a practical runbook for pre-QBR prep, in-meeting orchestration, and 30/60/90-day post-QBR follow-up.

Usage notes (quick):
- Treat this as a live template: copy -> tailor to account -> attach jira link for actions -> sync with AE 72h before
- Standard variant = 20–30 minute customer-facing presentation, mostly adoption-focused, one technical appendix.
- Enterprise variant = 45–60 minute executive + technical combined meeting with decision-focused agenda and explicit renewal negotiation asks.
- Colour and visuals are intentionally minimal to keep slide creation quick.

1) Slide slate (master outline) — common to both variants
- Cover / One-line summary: company, product footprint, renewal window, one-sentence QBR outcome ask.
  Speaker note: Start with 30s recap of relationship and your desired outcome today (e.g., alignment + next steps).
- Current Health Snapshot (1 slide): usage trend sparkline, adoption map (teams/features), top 3 wins since last QBR, top 3 open risks.
  Data placeholders: MRR impact, Avg latency / token cost signal (if relevant), 30-day active seats.
- Objectives & Success Metrics (1 slide): agreed success metrics (adoption, latency SLA, cost per 1k tokens, eval score), current vs target.
  Speaker note: Call out any metric that is off-track and why.
- Product / Delivery Roadmap (1 slide): planned improvements that affect account (model upgrades, quantization profiles, private deployment milestones).
  Speaker note: Map roadmap items to customer outcomes.
- Adoption Highlights (2 slides): quick case studies, customer stories, internal champions.
  Speaker note: Use screenshots or callouts if available.
- Risk & Mitigation Matrix (1 slide): risks mapped to impact and owner + actions.
  Example: "KV cache warmup time -> Impact: latency spikes -> Owner: eng-sre -> Action: enable per-route cache"
- Renewal & Commercial Snapshot (1 slide): current contract, renewal window, recommended renewal ask (upgrade/maintain/contract change), and proposed timeline.
  Distinguish Standard vs Enterprise language: Standard: "renewal recommendation + brief options"; Enterprise: "recommended commitment and negotiation levers (dedicated capacity, extended SLA)"
- Ask & Next Steps (1 slide): specific ask(s) with owners and dates.
- Appendix (3–6 slides): technical metrics, runbooks, integration notes, ticket backlog snapshot, exec bios.

2) Standard variant edits (compact)
- Trim to 7–9 slides total.
- Keep commercial slide simple: 3 options (renew in-place, apply 6–month pilot discount, scale to next tier).
- Use 1-page renewal tracker (see below) and make it the shared doc for AEs & CSMs.
- Meeting length: 20–30 minutes + 10 min for Q&A.
- Key attendees: CSM, AE, Customer Product Lead, optionally Technical Champion.

3) Enterprise variant edits (extended)
- Expand Risk & Mitigation to include SLO/infra design and data residency items.
- Add a "Decision Framework" slide: list contract levers, pricing levers, deployment levers and precedence.
- Add a "Negotiation Scenarios" slide: best-case / base-case / fallback with financial impact.
- Add a "Steering Committee" follow-up plan slide with names, meeting cadence, and evaluation criteria.
- Meeting length: 45–60 minutes (exec + tech breakout recommended).

4) One-page Renewal Tracker (copyable table as CSV lines below)
Columns: account, current_term_end, renewal_window_start, owner(csm/ae), recommended_action, next_meeting_date, risk_level, open_issues, agreement_status
Sample rows (CSV):
redwood-retailer,2025-02-28,2024-11-01,Aisha Patel / Daniel Kim,standard_renewal_no_change,2024-12-10,low,"latency spikes on peak hours (rt-1432)",in_discussion
vertex-bio,2025-04-15,2025-01-15,Renee Chu / Omar Basu,upgrade_to_dedicated,2025-02-20,high,"data residency + quantization evals pending (JIRA-CS-4789)",needs_exec_ok
little-learning-co,2024-12-01,2024-09-01,Diego Martinez / Sara Lin,pilot_extend_6m,2024-11-05,medium,"usage drop in embedding pipeline",proposal_sent

Tracker instructions: keep this tracker as a living sheet (CS folder), set follow-up tasks as tickets and link in open_issues field. Add a boolean "legal_review" flag in your local sheet if required.

5) QBR Prep runbook (timeline + owners)
- T-21 days: CSM to gather usage + incident summary, AE to confirm renewal window and any commercial levers. Create QBR draft slides.
- T-14 days: Draft review with Solutions Eng; check appendix metrics & infra notes. Raise any red flags.
- T-7 days: Run through with AE; align on Ask & alternatives. Confirm exec invites.
- T-3 days: Share final deck with customer and internal execs. Create JIRA tickets for post-QBR actions with initial owners and SLOs.
- Day of: Role play 15min pre-meeting (CSM + AE + SE). Run a 2-slide backup for executive-only meeting if tech absent.
- T+1 day: Send meeting notes and action tracker; update renewal tracker row.
- T+7 days: AE to follow up commercial items; CSM to drive adoption mitigations.
- T+30 / 60 / 90: update on action closure, impact to metrics, contract status.

6) Risk scoring rubric (simple)
- low: no open high-priority tickets, adoption trending up, renewal window >90 days.
- medium: 1–2 unresolved >S2 tickets, adoption flat/slow, renewal 60–90 days.
- high: unresolved S1/S0 issues or exec escalation, adoption dropping, renewal <60 days or execs undecided.

7) Talking points & scripts (short templates)
- Exec open (30s): "Thanks — quick 30s: we’ve seen X% increase in usage across Y teams and our work today is to agree on the next commitment that unlocks roadmap Z for you."
- Risk callout (20s): "We observed an intermittent latency increase tied to KV cache warmups; suggested mitigation is enabling per-route cache and a small auto-scaling buffer while we deploy the patch."
- Ask close (15s): "Our recommendation is a 12-month reserved capacity commit to ensure the latency SLA for your production traffic; can we align on timeline and next steps?"

8) Appendix templates (copy-paste elements)
- Ticket snapshot: JIRA key, short description, owner, status, eta.
- SLA impact table: metric, current state, target, remediation owner.
- Tech glossary for execs: brief definitions (dedicated, private, quantization, KV cache).

9) Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Create a slide pack variant for "technical deep-dive breakout" that can live as a 10-slide addon.
- Build a one-click deck generator (notebook) to pull last 90 days of usage + latency + cost curves. Logged as CONFLUENCE-1523.
- Need standardized visual for "adoption map" (product areas vs teams) — ask design for a template.

10) Quick checklist for CSM day-of
- [ ] Confirm attendees + exec backup 24h prior.
- [ ] Attach renewal tracker row to meeting invite.
- [ ] Load backup technical appendix in case of follow-up.
- [ ] Create JIRA action items during meeting with owners and 7-day follow-up.

11) Example annotated script for an Enterprise QBR (short)
- 0:00–0:05 Exec intro + relationships + one line summary of asks.
- 0:05–0:15 Health & adoption (CSM) + 3 wins.
- 0:15–0:25 Roadmap mapping and upcoming infra changes (PM/Eng).
- 0:25–0:35 Commercial & renewal scenarios (AE).
- 0:35–0:45 Technical risks & mitigation (Solutions Eng).
- 0:45–0:55 Decision & immediate next steps (all).

Bottom line / TL;DR (one sentence):
A two-track QBR template (compact for Standard, expanded for Enterprise) plus a short renewal sprint playbook that turns a meeting into a binding set of actions — focus on clean asks, a single living renewal tracker row, and measurable 30/60/90 follow-up.

Document history / notes:
- Drafted by: Aisha Patel 2024-10-03 (initial outline).
- Major revisions: 2024-12-02 (added tracker CSV examples), 2025-01-15 (added enterprise negotiation scenarios & prep runbook).

End of document.
